context_stem: Investment in evaluations: An inherent difficulty of an evaluations regime...
excerpt: Mid-training evaluations: For significant scale-ups, it may be necessary to perform evaluations mid-training. Such models may have capability limitations due to various (potentially slow or expensive) fine-tuning stages having not yet occurred, or because performance may not scale linearly with compute in the midst of training.
paraphrase: Significant scale-ups may require mid-training evaluations, though such models may have limitations from incomplete fine-tuning or nonlinear scaling.

context_stem: Investment in evaluations: An inherent difficulty of an evaluations regime...
excerpt: For now, we commit to perform mid-training fine-tuning and evaluations which, combined with the safety buffer described above, are intended to mitigate the risk of passing the defined ASL-3 threshold mid-training.
paraphrase: Anthropic commits to mid-training fine-tuning and evaluations, which with the safety buffer aim to mitigate the risk of exceeding ASL-3 mid-training.

context_stem: Investment in evaluations: An inherent difficulty of an evaluations regime...
excerpt: We expect to update our procedures in the future as we better understand how to perform mid-training evaluations, for example by adjusting task difficulty to account for the limitations of a mid-training model.
paraphrase: Procedures are expected to be updated as understanding of mid-training evaluations improves, such as adjusting task difficulty for mid-training limitations.

context_stem: Investment in evaluations: An inherent difficulty of an evaluations regime...
excerpt: At high safety levels, we may transition to doing full fine-tuning even for mid-training evals in order to further mitigate risks of underestimating capabilities.
paraphrase: At higher safety levels, full fine-tuning may be used even for mid-training evaluations to further reduce underestimation risk.

excerpt: Response policy: If an evaluation threshold triggers, we will follow the following procedure:
paraphrase: If an evaluation threshold is triggered, a defined response procedure will be followed.

context_stem: Response policy: If an evaluation threshold triggers, we will follow the following procedure:
excerpt: (1) If sufficient Containment Measures for the next ASL have already been implemented, ensure they are activated before continuing training.
paraphrase: If sufficient containment measures for the next ASL are already implemented, they must be activated before continuing training.

context_stem: Response policy: If an evaluation threshold triggers, we will follow the following procedure:
excerpt: (2) If sufficient measures are not yet implemented, pause training and analyze the level of risk presented by the model. In particular, conduct a thorough analysis to determine whether the evaluation was overly conservative, or whether the model indeed presents near-next-ASL risks.
paraphrase: If measures aren't ready, training is paused and the model's risk level is thoroughly analyzed to determine if the evaluation was overly conservative or the model genuinely poses near-next-ASL risk.

context_stem: Response policy: If an evaluation threshold triggers, we will follow the following procedure:
excerpt: (2a) If the evaluation is determined to be overly conservative (i.e. creating a greater than 6x "safety buffer") and the model is confirmed to not pose (or be close to posing) next-ASL risks, construct new evaluations that take into account this new information.
paraphrase: If the evaluation is found overly conservative (more than a 6x safety buffer) and the model doesn't pose near-next-ASL risk, new evaluations incorporating this information will be constructed.

context_stem: Response policy: If an evaluation threshold triggers, we will follow the following procedure:
excerpt: This document will be updated according to the "Update Process" described above before continuing training.
paraphrase: The document will be updated via the Update Process before training continues in this scenario.

context_stem: Response policy: If an evaluation threshold triggers, we will follow the following procedure:
excerpt: (2b) If the model is determined to be close to next-ASL risk, do not resume training until the next safety level has been defined (with this document updated accordingly) and its Containment Measures have been implemented.
paraphrase: If the model is close to next-ASL risk, training will not resume until the next safety level is defined and its containment measures implemented.

context_stem: Response policy: If an evaluation threshold triggers, we will follow the following procedure:
excerpt: (2c) If the model has already surpassed the next ASL during training, immediately lock down access to the weights. Stakeholders including the CISO and CEO should be immediately convened to determine whether the level of danger merits deletion of the weights.
paraphrase: If the model has already surpassed the next ASL during training, weight access is immediately locked down and the CISO, CEO, and other stakeholders convene to decide on possible weight deletion.

context_stem: Response policy: If an evaluation threshold triggers, we will follow the following procedure:
excerpt: After a detailed post-mortem, this policy should then be promptly updated to minimize risk of the re-occurrence of this failure (e.g. through more frequent or thorough evaluations).
paraphrase: Following a detailed post-mortem, the policy should be promptly updated to reduce recurrence risk, e.g. via more frequent or thorough evaluations.

context_stem: Response policy: If an evaluation threshold triggers, we will follow the following procedure:
excerpt: (2d) If it becomes apparent that the capabilities of a deployed model have been under-elicited and the model can, in fact, pass the evaluations, then we will halt further deployment to new customers and assess existing deployment cases for any serious risks which would constitute a safety emergency.
paraphrase: If a deployed model's capabilities were under-elicited and it actually passes the evaluations, deployment to new customers halts and existing deployments are assessed for safety emergencies.

context_stem: Response policy: If an evaluation threshold triggers, we will follow the following procedure:
excerpt: Given the safety buffer, de-deployment should not be necessary in the majority of deployment cases. If we identify a safety emergency, we will work rapidly to implement the minimum additional safeguards needed to allow responsible continued service to existing customers.
paraphrase: The safety buffer should make de-deployment rare; if a safety emergency is identified, minimum additional safeguards will be rapidly implemented to allow continued service.

context_stem: Response policy: If an evaluation threshold triggers, we will follow the following procedure:
excerpt: We will provide transparency and support to impacted customers throughout the process. An emergency of this type would merit a detailed post-mortem and a policy shift to avoid re-occurrence of this situation.
paraphrase: Anthropic will provide transparency and support to affected customers, and such an emergency would trigger a detailed post-mortem and policy change to prevent recurrence.
